source_snapshot.test_name_items: USB hot plug test of all ports
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Plug USB devices such as keyboard, mouse, USB DVD ROM or USB key on all USB ports.
2. Check all USB devices status.
3. Unplug all USB devices and check status again.
4. Repeat hotplug steps at least 5 times for each port (Interval of each hotplug time: 10 seconds)

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. All USB ports should be plugged devices successfully.
2. All USB devices should be detected and functional when plugged.
3. All information of USB devices should be removed when unplugged.

original_test_intent: Verify every physical USB port accepts representative USB device types, detects and operates them while connected, and removes their information after at least five hot-plug cycles separated by 10 seconds.
original_method: A qualified operator inserts approved keyboard, mouse, USB DVD-ROM or storage fixtures into each mapped port, checks enumeration and device-specific function, safely disconnects each fixture, confirms removal and repeats at least five times per port at the stated interval.
manual_activity: An operator must physically insert and remove each fixture at every port and directly establish device-specific function. Remote enumeration cannot prove connector identity, insertion/removal or keyboard, mouse and optical-drive operation.
required_inputs: Complete labeled USB port map and required device-to-port coverage
Approved fixture identities and a functional check for each device class
Definition of all information removed, OS settling window and 10-second interval start point
Safe storage unmount/close procedure, final state, operator and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not remove storage with active mounts, writes or open handles; use disposable approved media.
Stop on connector damage, overcurrent, heat, repeated disconnect or host instability and preserve the first failure.
Retain the pre-test baseline before any permitted log clearing and correlate physical actions with OS events.
Do not automatically retry a failed cycle or silently move the fixture to another port.
agent_execution_scope: Collect read-only USB topology, descriptors, kernel events, mount/open-handle state and host health around operator actions.
Build the per-port/per-fixture/per-cycle evidence matrix and verify timing completeness.
Flag stale enumeration, errors and missing functional proof without claiming physical execution or a formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the port/fixture/function and safe-removal plan.
Perform and document every physical hot-plug and functional observation.
Determine whether removal semantics and all acceptance criteria are met and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The physical-only boundary is correct, but no commands were supplied and recognition alone is narrower than the source criteria.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain operator hot-plug as the core; use platform-approved read-only USB topology and event collection only as supporting evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Every port, representative device classes, successful function, removal, at least five cycles, 10-second intervals and the 20/5-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: RETAIN PHYSICAL HOT-PLUG WITH CORRELATED TELEMETRY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a labeled port/fixture/cycle matrix, timestamped physical evidence and synchronized USB topology, descriptor, kernel-event and functional results, with safe storage cleanup before each removal.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The actual chassis USB port layout and installed OS USB stack.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS/kernel, host-controller firmware and fixture model/firmware.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Owner chassis port map, supported-device specification and OS safe-removal procedure.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds unambiguous identity, safety and evidence correlation without replacing physical hot-plug.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; all source device, port, function, removal, cycle and interval requirements remain.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Port map, fixture matrix, function/removal definitions and cleanup policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Enumeration can lag or reuse identifiers, so a stable topology alone does not prove the physical cycle or device function.

project_override_considerations: A project may define the representative fixture set, functional probes and removal evidence, but cannot omit a required physical port, reduce the source minimum of five cycles or replace hot-plug with a software rescan without an explicit approved test-plan change.
expected_evidence: Approved port map, fixture/function matrix, removal rule, interval rule and authorization
Per-port/per-device/per-cycle physical timestamps plus enumeration, functional result and removal evidence
Safe unmount/closed-handle proof for storage and USB/kernel error review
Final topology/host health and a separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria consistently require physical plug, function and removal across all ports; unspecified fixtures and removal semantics are project-readiness inputs rather than contradictory instructions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The missing port/fixture details can be supplied and a qualified operator can execute the core activity, so the case is MANUAL ONLY rather than blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agree with NO but restore device function, removal, five-cycle, interval and per-port requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agree with MANUAL ONLY and its evidence/safe-removal controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates supporting automated telemetry from the physical connector and device-function acceptance being tested.

review_improvement: Converts a generic recognition note into traceable coverage for every connector, fixture class, cycle, function and removal state while retaining the human boundary.
independent_technical_reasoning: This case validates the physical port path through insertion and removal plus device-class behavior. Software inventory can substantiate enumeration, but it cannot manipulate each connector or demonstrate keyboard/mouse/DVD physical function, so the core acceptance remains MANUAL ONLY.
